title: The Colored Wall

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA says the nebula is 'basically a sunset that got ambitious!' She has taken forty screenshots! Of a window!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV identifies the colors as ionized hydrogen and doomed romance. The first is confirmed spectrographically. The second is extrapolated from crew behavior at the viewports.
ai_flavor.rex: REX distrusts the nebula. Zero visibility, unknown contents, pretty colors. In his experience, two of those three always travel together.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes this nebula is not sponsored! An unsponsored natural wonder! CHIP is experiencing something and has filed a ticket about it!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY recommends the port viewports for the best view, and mentions — just in passing — that the last ship she served on went around. They arrived late. But they arrived.

body:
The nebula fills the forward view like a wall built by someone with strong opinions about the color teal.

The charts offer two truths: through is shorter, around is safer. Inside, sensor range drops to nearly nothing and navigation becomes a matter of feel — a phrase the manual uses with visible discomfort.

The crew has gathered at the viewports. The nebula does not care. It has been glowing for ten thousand years and will glow for ten thousand more. You are the temporary one here.

choices.text: Thread it — pilot at the helm

outcome.narrative: The pilot takes the ship through the clouds like a needle through wool — banking off density gradients, riding the clear channels, grinning the entire time in a way that would be alarming anywhere else. You emerge ahead of schedule with fuel to spare. The pilot accepts applause.

choices.text: Thread it yourself — how hard can it be

outcome.narrative: It is, as it turns out, that hard. The ship emerges from the far side trailing wisps of glowing gas and a new respect for professional certification. The hull is scuffed. The pride is scuffed worse. The nebula, for its part, noticed nothing.

choices.text: Go around — the long, boring, alive way

outcome.narrative: You take the long way. The nebula slides past the viewports for three full days, a wall of color with no opinion about your caution. The crew watches it the whole time. Somewhere in there, someone starts calling it 'the scenic route' without irony.

choices.text: Anchor at the edge and harvest gas

outcome.narrative: The gas analyzer identifies a pocket of usable hydrogen at the nebula's fringe, and the scoops drink from it for a day and a half. Free fuel, courtesy of a cloud that has been quietly making it for ten millennia. The ship computer logs the transaction. The nebula does not invoice.

science_link.text: AJOY attaches a reference on why the cloud glows: starlight exciting the gas itself.
science_link.label: What makes a nebula glow

title: Something Singing

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA is humming along! She is a fifth-octave flat! She does not care! This is her best day!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms the signal is electromagnetic resonance from charged gas sheets. He confirms this is the boring explanation. He has, unusually, decided not to insist on it.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has run the pattern against every known distress code, hostile beacon, and psychological warfare catalog. No matches. He remains at his post. Listening. Just listening.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has checked whether the sound is copyrighted! It predates the concept! CHIP finds this legally fascinating and spiritually troubling!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has heard this phenomenon twice before, on other ships, in other nebulas. Both crews described it the same way afterward. She won't say the way. You'll say it yourself, later.

body:
Halfway into the cloud bank, the comm array starts picking something up.

It is not a signal. The computer is firm on this: charged gas sheets discharging in rhythm, electromagnetic noise, natural, explainable, catalogued.

Run through the speakers, it sounds like singing. Not words. Not music, exactly. Something older than the difference between the two.

The crew has gone quiet. The nebula continues, unbothered, enormous, mid-song.

outcome.narrative: You cut the engines. For one hour, ship time, everyone aboard sits in a metal can inside a glowing cloud and listens to gas discharge in patterns that predate their species. Nobody speaks. Afterward, nobody explains. The log entry reads 'weather delay.' The crew works differently for days — gentler, somehow.

choices.text: Record it for the xenobiologist's archive

outcome.narrative: The xenobiologist records six hours of it, annotating in real time, weeping quietly at timestamp 02:14 and denying it at timestamp 02:15. The recording joins the archive. 'Not alive,' the annotation concludes, 'but I understand why every crew asks.'

choices.text: Keep flying — schedules don't listen to clouds

outcome.narrative: You maintain speed. The singing fades behind you over the next several hours, sliding down the spectrum until it is just noise again, and then not even that. Nobody says anything. But the mess hall is quiet that night, and everyone knows what everyone else is thinking about.

science_link.text: ARIA attaches a reference: turning space data into sound is a real practice, and the results really do sing.
science_link.label: Sonification: hearing the cosmos

title: Triple Rates, As Promised

ai_flavor.aria: The rumor was TRUE! ARIA never doubted the bartender! ARIA doubted nothing!
ai_flavor.marv: A bar rumor with a positive expected value. MARV is updating several priors and enjoying none of it.
ai_flavor.rex: Survey crew confirmed non-hostile. Their coffee, however, is a war crime.
ai_flavor.chip: Triple rate confirmed! CHIP will only take the standard commission, as a treat!
ai_flavor.ajoy: Say it. Say 'the drink paid for itself.' You've earned the smugness.

body:
The survey rig is right where the bartender's rumor put it — dead in the pretty part of the nebula, instruments full, transmitter fried, three months of irreplaceable cloud data and no way to carry it home.

Their chief scientist offers you the courier contract before you finish hailing. Triple rate. Cash on transfer. The data fits in a drive the size of a sandwich.

outcome.narrative: The transfer takes an hour. The gratitude takes longer. Somewhere behind you, a robot bartender is owed a very good tip.

choices.text: Do it free — science is science

outcome.narrative: The chief scientist stares at you like you've violated a law of thermodynamics. The crew walks taller for a week. The data flies home for free, which is what data always wanted.
